title: Release Railgun — Canary Safeguard and LTS Channel Mapper for Private Upgrades
creator: Sofia Park
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, policy-driven 'Release Railgun' service that coordinates canary rollouts and LTS channel mapping for Redwood Private customers. The service should: 1) map incoming cluster metadata to appropriate LTS/compat channels; 2) orchestrate staged canary cohorts with configurable gate rules (observability thresholds, health probes, rollback windows); 3) manage sequenced migration jobs (schema + state translations) with idempotent checkpoints and pause/resume hooks; 4) provide dry-run and preflight probes that validate binary + schema compatibility without touching production state. This ticket covers the core orchestration layer, policy DSL, and the migration job sequencing primitives for VPC/on-prem deployments. Implementation must be compatible with existing private control plane agents and fit into the Private upgrade playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Railgun service can accept a cluster manifest and return the LTS channel recommendation (stable, maintenance, legacy) based on semantic-version rules and installed operator versions.
Define a policy DSL for canary cohorts including: cohort size, metric thresholds (error rate, p99 latency, token throughput), minimum observation window, and automatic rollback triggers.
Sequenced migration runner supports transactional steps with idempotent checkpoints and a resume command that recovers mid-flight after failure without reapplying completed steps.
Dry-run preflight verifies model binary compatibility, schema compatibility, and cluster resource checks (GPU/CPU/memory) and emits a human-readable report with remediation hints.
Integration tests that simulate canary progression across three cohorts and demonstrate automatic rollback when a cohort breaches thresholds.
Documentation and runbook added to Confluence with example policies and a troubleshooting checklist for SREs and field engineers.

notes: Trade-offs considered: saga/event-driven runner vs deterministic state-stepper. Chosen: state-stepper because it provides deterministic replay and is easier to reason about for air-gapped clusters.
We will support both semantic version mapping and component-compat heuristics (operator versions, runtime kernel IDs) to decide LTS channel recommendation.
Rollout policy defaults: 1% -> 10% -> 50% cohorts with 30m observation windows, but customers can opt into fast-path or manual gating.
Migration artifacts will be signed and uploaded to customer-visible artifact registry when available; Railgun will request short-lived KMS decrypt tokens from control-plane agent to run checks.

Plan for backwards compatibility: when encountering unknown manifests, Railgun returns a 'manual-review' channel and emits a preflight checklist for field engineers rather than attempting automated migration.
